name: Vulvovaginal Gingival Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Vulvovaginal Gingival Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of desquamative gingivitis, vulvar erosions, and vaginal mucosal involvement
Histopathological evidence of lichenoid interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration
Direct immunofluorescence showing linear fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane zone
Exclusion of other causes of desquamative gingivitis and vulvovaginal erosions such as pemphigoid and lupus erythematosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of the clinical triad (desquamative gingivitis, vulvar and vaginal mucosal involvement) plus histopathological confirmation of lichenoid interface dermatitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Direct immunofluorescence is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis requires exclusion of other mucocutaneous autoimmune diseases.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of tumor necrosis factor secretion

laboratory: Histopathology showing lichenoid interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration
Direct immunofluorescence demonstrating linear fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane zone
Negative serology for pemphigoid and lupus erythematosus antibodies
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound may be used to assess vaginal stenosis or scarring
genetic: No known genetic mutations identified; considered autoimmune in etiology
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic mucosal erosions and desquamation
Response to immunosuppressive therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of subepithelial blistering on histology
Linear IgG and C3 deposition on direct immunofluorescence
Absence of vulvovaginal scarring typical in vulvovaginal gingival syndrome
Positive ANA and other lupus-specific antibodies
Systemic symptoms such as arthritis and renal involvement
Histology showing interface dermatitis with immune complex deposition

redFlags: Rapid progression of vaginal stenosis causing urinary or sexual dysfunction
Severe mucosal ulcerations with secondary infection
Ocular involvement leading to conjunctival scarring or vision impairment
references: Chan LS, Ahmed AR, Anhalt GJ, et al. The first international consensus on mucous membrane pemphigoid: definition, diagnostic criteria, pathogenic factors, medical treatment, and prognostic indicators. Arch Dermatol. 2002;138(3):370-379.
Scully C, Carrozzo M. Oral mucosal diseases: Lichen planus. Br J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2008;46(1):15-21.
Fitzpatrick TB, Johnson RA, Wolff K, et al. Fitzpatrick's Dermatology in General Medicine. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2012.
